DR. HENRY EDWIN BRYANJ _July 4, 1973_ 

## Dear Dr. Bryan, 

I’ve been out of the U.S., as the enclosed article tells; I took you at your word that you wanted me to enclose a note. My check for the $100 that I owe you will be delayed a little longer, because emergency surgery on my lower jaw suddenly ate up all that we had on hand financially (no pun intended), but it will come as soon as we get our next royalty check. I think of you often, and am glad to at least find your address and be able to get it all together enough to tell you that I’ve failed to pay you because I’ve been desperately broke, due to my depres­ sion which prevented me from doing any writing of novels or stories—the girl Francie to whom I was engaged, whom you may recall, abruptly moved out, leav­ ing me with little or no reason for either writing or living. I abandoned my home in San Rafael and all my possessions and went to Canada; I had been invited to come there to speak at the University of British Colombia [sic
summary:
—my spelling is as bad as ever ... and there I tried suicide, after finding that I had no friends at all and was living in a foreign country, more alienated than ever before. But then, as the article tells, I was invited to fly down here to Fullerton, which is near Disney­ land, and did so, and met a dear girl who is now my wife. We are expecting a baby soon, and are very happy. Tessa is warm and kind and loving, and has healed for me many of the scars of the past. And, which is very good, I am writ­ ing again, as the article tells. My fame and reputation especially in France and Germany and England has grown so that I am invited to go there, but the baby’s arrival prevents that for now. I am off drugs of all kinds, and glad of it. I miss, though, many of my heavy 
doper friends—those who lived through their dope trips and those who did not— and have written them into my novel, mentioned in the article. 

Please bear with me a little longer about the money; I am at last just getting back on my feet financially, but the cost of the baby, the hospital and doctor bills, etc., takes it right away, and I want to be sure my wife is protected. I think of you often, and I wish I could consult with you again, but alas, I am 600 miles away, far too far. I live a straight life now; no one here knows that once I was a hippie doper (as they would put it) ... and yet I grieve for the loss of my former wife and the child of that marriage, whom I would very much like to see but can’t. Anyhow...
